primitives.name: Foot Placement Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: PREPARING THE MATERIAL 79 PASSING TO PLAYER FOR LINE PLUNGE The quarter back in passing to the full back for a line plunge through the center should, if the full back is going through on the right side, bring his right foot back almost behind his left.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ_f': 'angle of foot placement relative to centerline (radians)', 'd_f': 'distance between feet (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Quarterback maintains stable base; fullback moves laterally toward center.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Foot alignment deviates beyond ±15° from optimal.

layer2.mapping: Quadratic relationship between foot angle deviation and pass efficiency; inverse correlation with receiver blocking effectiveness.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation of quarterback's rear foot from center axis during pass.

primitives.name: Ball Trajectory Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ball should be placed low, in the pit of the stomach with the right hand.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'h_b': 'height of ball release above ground (meters)', 'v_b': 'vertical velocity component (m/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball released at optimal horizontal velocity; receiver positioned for low catch.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball height exceeds waist level, reducing receiver control.

layer2.mapping: Minimizes vertical velocity component to ensure low trajectory; enables faster receiver acceleration.
layer2.telemetry: Vertical displacement of ball at reception point relative to waist.

primitives.name: Receiver Hand Positioning
primitives.verbatim_quote: The full back should not reach for the ball with his hands but should carry them almost by his side and grasp the ball instantly as the quarter back places it against his body.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ_h': 'hand angle relative to body (radians)', 't_r': 'reaction time to ball contact (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Receiver maintains passive posture until contact; quarterback delivers precise placement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Hand extension beyond 30° from body midline causes misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Inverse correlation between hand extension and pass accuracy; reduces interference risk.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation of receiver’s hands from body axis at ball contact.

Ball trajectory optimization enforces low release heights to maximize receiver control and minimize interception risk. Receiver hand positioning prevents premature motion that could disrupt pass timing. These elements form a coherent system where each action influences the next: proper foot alignment allows for accurate low-pass delivery, which in turn requires precise receiver readiness. Failure modes include excessive foot spread, high ball release, or extended hands—each introducing inefficiencies or errors in execution. The interplay of these variables creates a deterministic yet adaptive structure for line plunges.
